thread.title: Stock Market Rises; Bank Of America, Goldman, Netflix, Lululemon In Focus: Weekly Review

author: IBD STAFF
title: Stock Market Rises; Bank Of America, Goldman, Netflix, Lululemon In Focus: Weekly Review
text:
The stock market rally continued, with the Dow Jones, S&P 500 index and Nasdaq composite clearing their 50-day moving averages. Netflix ( NFLX ) gave weak Q1 guidance but shares rose for the week on a subscription price hike. Bank stocks boomed on earnings results, notably Bank of America ( BAC ) and Goldman Sachs ( GS ), and they stressed in earnings calls that the economy seems to be in good shape. Some airline and rail earnings came out, while a number of retailers and restaurants gave preliminary figures, including Lululemon Athletica ( LULU ). Other top stocks broke out past buy zones.
X
Stock Market Rally Clears Resistance The Dow Jones, S&P 500 index and Nasdaq continued to rally in the latest week on hints of China trade talks progress, shrugging off the government shutdown and Brexit uncertainty. The Nasdaq staged its own follow-through day and reclaimed its 50-day line. The S&P 500, which confirmed the market rally back on Jan. 4, moved above its 50-day line on Thursday along with the Dow Jones. Beaten-down banks were big winners on earnings. More top stocks broke out of bullish bases, with many more setting up. Crude oil prices rallied.
Netflix Earnings Guidance Disappoints Netflix beat its forecast for new subscribers in the fourth quarter, but disappointed with its current-quarter outlook. The subscription video-on-demand service added 8.8 million paying subscribers in the December quarter, bringing its worldwide total to 139.3 million. Netflix had forecast 7.6 million. It earned 30 cents a share, beating views by six cents, while revenue of $4.19 billion just missed. For the current quarter, Netflix expects to add 8.9 million paying subscribers and earn 56 cents on sales of $4.49 billion. Wall Street was modeling EPS of 83 cents on sales of $4.61 billion. Shares fell 4% Friday, but rose slightly for the week. Earlier in the week, Netflix raised its monthly subscription rates in the U.S. by 13% to 18%.
Banks Say Economy Still Strong Executives from Citigroup ( C ), JPMorgan ( JPM ) and Bank of America ( BAC ) said that underlying economic trends remained strong, belying the market spasms over trade friction and fears of a recession. But JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned that the U.S. government shutdown could reduce economic growth to "zero" during the first quarter if it dragged on, and urged greater cooperation among U.S. leaders. JPMorgan's Q4 results were mixed. So were results from Wells Fargo ( WFC ) and Citigroup. Results from Bank of America and Goldman Sachs ( GS ) breezed past estimates. Goldman also apologized over a banker's role in the 1MDB scandal. Morgan Stanley ( MS ) results missed.
Atlassian Earnings Boom Atlassian ( TEAM ) reported fiscal Q2 profit and revenue that topped expectations. Shares spiked to record highs Friday but reversed lower. The maker of project-management and collaborative software earned 25 cents a share, up 92% vs. a year earlier, the third straight quarter of accelerating growth. Revenue rose 39% to $299 million. Q2 billings rose 49%, topping estimates of 34% growth as Atlassian benefited from pull-forward of maintenance contract renewals before pricing increases went into effect in early October. For the March quarter, Atlassian forecast profit in line with analyst estimates. It expects revenue of $304 million, slightly above estimates of $301 million.
Delta Warns On shutdown; United Bullish Delta Air Lines ( DAL ) warned that lower government-related travel resulting from the government shutdown would weigh on first-quarter unit revenue, which it expects to slow from Q4. Still, the carrier said the travel-demand environment was "solid" and that it was well-equipped to handle swings in fuel prices and a potential economic downturn. Fourth-quarter results were mixed. United Airlines ( UAL ) easily beat Q4 forecasts but also forecast slowing Q1 revenue. The carrier said it had not "detected much of an impact" from the geopolitical stresses weighing on markets.
Meanwhile, Irish budget carrier Ryanair ( RYAAY ) tumbled Friday after cutting 2019 profit guidance on weak winter fares. It said further cuts could depend on how Brexit plays out.
Lululemon Sees Strong Holiday Sales IBD 50 stock Lululemon ( LULU ) jumped after the firm raised its Q4 guidance on better-than-expected holiday sales. Meanwhile Crocs ( CROX ) slipped despite upping guidance, while Boot Barn ( BOOT ) surged after posting sales figures that came above expectations. American Eagle Outfitters ( AEO ) also beat on sales and reaffirmed its Q4 guidance. In contrast, Abercrombie & Fitch ( ANF ) tumbled after saying Q4 net sales will decrease, despite Q4 comparable-store sales increasing in the low-single digits. IBD 50 stock Five Below ( FIVE ) regained some ground after initially slipping on a 4.9% holiday sales comp increase. Tailored Brands ( TLRD ) stock collapsed after it said it expects same-store sales for Jos. A. Bank stores to be flat vs. prior guidance for a low-single-digit increase. Finally, department store chain Nordstrom ( JWN ) tanked after it reported disappointing holiday sales. Tiffany ( TIF ) and Signet Jewelers ( SIG ) also warned on the holiday quarter.
UnitedHealth Earnings Beat On Optum UnitedHealth ( UNH ), the nation's largest insurer, powered past Wall Street earnings estimates thanks to the growth of its Optum division. EPS grew 27% to $3.28 as revenue rose 12% to $58.4 billion. Optum, which combines health services, prescription benefit management and technology services, accounted for 60% of operating profit, up from 55% a year ago. UnitedHealth stock shook off concerns about elevated Medicaid expenses, which management said was a short-term issue.
Rail Operators Deliver Growth CSX ( CSX ) saw EPS vault 58% to $1.01, meeting views. Revenue beat, rising 10% to $3.143 billion. Operating efficiency missed some metrics, despite recent improvements from the rail giant adopting the "precision railroading" strategy. The rail giant also sees 2019 revenue growth in the "low single-digits," amid concerns about global growth and trade. CSX stock fell after the report but rose solidly for the week. Regional player Kansas City Southern ( KSU ) on Friday posted in-line EPS of $1.56, up 13%, on revenue of $694 million, up 5%. Shares gapped up Friday to retake the 200-day line for the first time since October. Canadian Pacific ( CP ) reports Wednesday and Union Pacific ( UNP ) has an earnings call early Thursday.
Schwab Earnings Jump 48% Charles Schwab ( SCHW ) saw fourth-quarter EPS vault 48% to 65 cents. Revenue climbed 19% to $2.669 billion. Both beat modestly. Net interest revenue and trading revenue jumped in Q4, but fee-based revenue fell 13%. Daily average trades surged 38%, but average revenue per trade fell 3%. Shares surged for the week, extending a recent rally above the 50-day line. Rival online brokers Interactive Brokers ( IBKR ) and TD Ameritrade ( AMTD ) report Tuesday. E-Trade ( ETFC ) earnings follow Thursday.
Ford Cuts Q4 Views As VW Pact Disappoints No. 2 U.S. automaker Ford ( F ) warned Q4 will be weaker than expected and it now sees Q4 EPS of 30 cents and full-year 2018 EPS of $1.30, both below estimates. Ford, which reports Wednesday, also offered a cloudy 2019 outlook, citing tariff costs and Brexit uncertainty. Analysts said that could add to Ford's difficulties in building investors' confidence around its turnaround plan. The gloom contrasts with the recent bullish 2019 forecast from General Motors ( GM ). Meanwhile, Ford and Volkswagen ( VWAGY ) announced earlier at the Detroit auto show an alliance built around commercial trucks and vans. A highly anticipated pact on electric and self-driving cars went missing, though the companies reported talks are progressing. Meanwhile, Chinese electric vehicle maker Kandi Technologies ( KNDI ) said it plans to export two EVs to the U.S. this year.
Tesla ( TSLA ) said it will cut 7% of full-time staff as it tries to increase Model 3 production, making cheaper versions that will squeeze profits. CEO Elon Musk warned of a "very difficult" road ahead. Tesla stock tumbled Friday.
Marijuana Stocks Tilray ( TLRY ) stock sold off after the Canadian cannabis producer's IPO lockup expired. This came even though it announced a revenue-sharing deal to produce CBD products in the U.S. and globally with Authentic Brands. Meanwhile rival marijuana stock Canopy Growth ( CGC ) jumped after New York granted the Canadian firm a license to produce hemp on an industrial scale in the state. Finally, Attorney General nominee William Barr has said he will not "go after" cannabis companies operating in states where it is legal.
Restaurants Serve Up Guidance Wingstop ( WING ) fell after preliminary fourth-quarter results showed slowing sales growth. Total sales increased 15% vs. 15.1% in Q3. Dave & Buster's ( PLAY ) expects Q4 same-store sales to rise 1.8%-2.5% with full-year revenue of $1.26 billion. Denny's ( DENN ) expects Q4 revenue of $157.1 million, below consensus. Del Taco ( TACO ) now sees 2018 revenue of $505.3 million and 2019 revenue of $515-$527 million, both below views. The restaurant chains offered initial Q4 results on the sidelines of an industry conference.
News In Brief Edwards Lifesciences ( EW ) and Boston Scientific ( BSX ) agreed to settle all litigation related to heart-valve replacements, valve-repair devices and closure devices. Edwards will pay Boston $180 million. Shares of both companies rose on the news.
Fiserv ( FISV ) will acquire payment processor First Data ( FDC ) for $22 billion in stock, spurring more fintech consolidation speculation. One view is that Fidelity National Information Services ( FIS ) could pursue Total System Services ( TSS ). Fiserv could invest more in First Data's Clover startup, pressuring Square ( SQ ), analysts said.
PG&E ( PCG ) said it plans to file for bankruptcy protection as the California utility faces potential liabilities of more than $30 billion from recent massive wildfires. Shares, already down sharply in recent months, crashed.
Newmont Mining ( NEM ) will buy Goldcorp ( GG ) in a $10 billion deal, following Barrick Gold ( ABX ) buying Randgold for $5.4 billion late last year.
Snap ( SNAP ) CFO Tim Stone quit after less than a year. The Snapchat operator said Q4 results would come in at the high end of its guidance, but shares plunged.
Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) reported Q4 sales of $9.4 billion, but revenue guidance for the current quarter was well below views. TSM is a contract chip manufacturer, and its two top clients, Apple ( AAPL ) and Huawei, are struggling.
J.B. Hunt ( JBHT ) stock popped after it beat earnings expectations in Q3. However the freight shipping and trucking company faces rising costs due to a shortage of truckers.
American Express ( AXP ) missed Q4 earnings views and gave a cautious outlook on 2019 earnings. AmEx stock reversed to close up 1% Friday, capping a solid week for the Dow Jones component.
Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Walgreens Boots Alliance ( WBA ) announced a wide-ranging strategic partnership, the latest Microsoft cloud alliance with a big company. The pharmacy chain will use Microsoft's cloud computing software and services and the two firms plan to innovate in the health care space.
